observations:
Torah #71 is a two-paragraph aphoristic teaching — the briefest Torah in Likutey Moharan. The source text contains one unified conceptual domain with no independently branching bechina families.

The threshold for a new package is: 3+ concepts with explicit bechina language forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages.

All bechina-language concepts identified in Torah #71 belong to one domain: the publicly-known tzaddik (מְפֻרְסָם) who bears suffering on behalf of the masses (יִסּוּרִין בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּים), identified with Isaiah 53 ('לָכֵן אֲחַלֶּק לוֹ בָרַבִּים' / 'וּבַחֲבֻרָתוֹ נִרְפָּא לָנוּ'), extended in Paragraph 2 to the voluntary form (מְקַבְּלִים יִסּוּרִים בִּשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל / מַחֲלִיפִין הַשֶּׁפַע). These six nodes form one single tightly-bounded bechina cluster, which becomes Package 1. There is no second independent domain.

Two potential second-package candidates were examined and rejected:

1. CANDIDATE: A 'שֶׁפַע / divine flow / exchange' package built around מַחֲלִיפִין הַשֶּׁפַע.
   REJECTION: מַחֲלִיפִין הַשֶּׁפַע appears in a single clause of a single sentence ('וּבָזֶה מַחֲלִיפִין הַשֶּׁפַע') that is inseparably bound to the suffering-on-behalf-of-Israel context. There are no other concepts in Torah #71 that are given bechina-identity within a שֶׁפַע/flow domain. The exchange of divine flow is not developed as an independent conceptual family in this Torah — it is the named outcome of the voluntary-suffering concept, and belongs within Package 1. A package requires 3+ bechina-connected nodes forming an independent domain; the שֶׁפַע domain has exactly one node in this Torah.

2. CANDIDATE: An 'Isaiah 53 / Suffering Servant' package grouping the two verse-nodes.
   REJECTION: Both verse-nodes ('לָכֵן אֲחַלֶּק לוֹ בָרַבִּים' and 'וּבַחֲבֻרָתוֹ נִרְפָּא לָנוּ') are bechina-equivalents of מְפֻרְסָם and יִסּוּרִין respectively — they are the verse-expressions of the same essential nature already captured by those two nodes. They are within Package 1's domain, not an independent package. A package of 'Isaiah-53 verses' would be a thematic categorization by biblical source, not by shared bechina-nature — which would violate the framework's rule that packages represent shared essential nature, not shared textual origin.

STRUCTURAL NOTE: Torah #71's brevity is itself significant for the graph. It is the Rebbe's most compressed teaching — two paragraphs, one idea, no elaborate apparatus of letters/sefirot/rabbinic characters. This teaching functions as an annotation or corollary to Torah #63 (explicitly cross-referenced at the end of Paragraph 2). Torah #71 should be understood as adding a single conceptual node-cluster to the larger graph centered on Isaiah 53's theology of the tzaddik who absorbs communal suffering, which can then serve as a bridge to Torah #63's fuller treatment of the same theme (the Seraph who covers his face with two wings, in the context of the tzaddik mediating between Israel and Heaven).

Conclusion: Package 1 (מְפֻרְסָם וְיִסּוּרִין בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּים) accounts for all bechina-connected concepts in Torah #71. No new independent package is warranted.
